analysis.title: China Economic Activity and Policy Tracker: Nov 20
key_insights: GS now publishes the China activity tracker weekly instead of less often, to follow the effect of the higher energy price supply shock on Chinese economic activity.
GS China GDP nowcast fell to 4.5% yoy for Q4 after weak October activity data.
30-city primary-market property transaction volume fell over the past week, as did 16-city secondary-market volume.
NBS 70-city and Centaline 6-city secondary home prices were largely flat in October, and rental yields in large cities were largely flat in October.
Domestic passenger flights edged down over the past week, the flight cancellation rate was broadly stable, and traffic congestion ticked up.
Brent oil price declined over the past week while domestic gasoline and diesel prices were unchanged. Chemical prices edged down broadly.
GS nowcast of China oil demand increased to 17.0mb/d in the latest reading.
Steel demand was stable and steel production edged up over the past week. Daily coal consumption in coastal provinces was largely stable.
RMB 4.13tn of local government special bonds have been issued year-to-date, matching the year-ago level. Government bond issuance reached RMB10.6tn, or 89% of the annual quota.
Seasonally adjusted EPMI declined in November, and Morning Consult consumer confidence declined over the past week.
Official port container throughput declined over the past week but stayed above year-ago levels. Freight volume of departing ships at 20 major ports fell.
Outstanding US soybean export sales to China for the 2026/27 marketing year ticked down in the second week of November.
Rare earth magnet export volume to the EU and US fell in October, while volume to Japan edged up.
Overnight interbank repo rates edged down over the past week. The CDB-CGB yield spread widened to 11 bps.
CNY was largely flat against USD but appreciated against the CFETS basket. The single-month FX conversion ratio for the goods trade balance rose to 74% in October.
The USDCNY fixing-implied countercyclical factor was largely flat over the last week, and onshore LGFV credit spreads widened sharply over the last week.
On Nov 3 the PBOC raised the RRR for FX deposits by 2pp, signaling discomfort over rapid RMB appreciation. On Oct 31 it changed its policy rate from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate.
